findings.claim: FR-WS-007 AC-5 requires each stalled session sender thread to be released within 2 s after its write blocked (writeTimeout 1 s), but the TinyHttpd test asserts <= 3000 ms for both the session end and the longest blocked write, so the 2 s bound of the AC is not demonstrated and a regression between 2 s and 3 s passes. The lane review left this open as R2-004.
findings.evidence: NaruServe-tinyhttpd/src/test/java/com/snoworca/naruserve/tinyhttpd/WebSocketSendSocketTest.java:234 and :239 (comment at :212-214); AC in docs/spec/11.websocket.srs.md FR-WS-007 AC-5
findings.suggested_fix: Assert <= 2000 (with a slack figure written into the AC if a loaded host needs one) or amend FR-WS-007 AC-5 to state the 3 s bound and its reason.

findings.claim: FR-WS-008 VE-9 (covers AC-6) cites sdsAc10_FR_WS_008_AC6_pingsDoNotResetTheIdleClock, which does not exist; the test is named sdsAc10_FR_WS_008_AC4_pingsDoNotResetTheIdleClock and exercises AC-4 (pings are no activity), not AC-6. AC-6 stays covered by VE-8, but the trace pointer is unresolvable and misattributed.
findings.suggested_fix: Correct VE-9 to the existing method name and change Covers to AC-4 through the SRS MCP evidence tools.

findings.claim: The close-wait timing half of the FR-WS-010 AC-1 reserved-session test is guarded by Assume.assumeTrue(releaseMs <= 600), so on a slow host the check that the wait ends on the reserved session close (not on the 1 s timeout) is skipped silently inside a test the SRS cites as passing.
findings.suggested_fix: Fail or retry instead of skipping, or move the timing assertions to their own test whose setup controls the release time.
